title: Phonon-Bottleneck-Governed Ultrafast Hot-Carrier Super-Diffusion in Transition Metal Dichalcogenides
authors: Yuwei Zhang, Dongyang Wan, Tao Zhou, Hao Wu, Junpeng Lu, Zhenhua Ni
abstract: Two-dimensional transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDCs) are promising for low-power optoelectronics, yet their operational speed is widely considered constrained by low room-temperature mobilities and carrier transit delays. Here, by combining on-chip terahertz optoelectronic sampling with thermally evaporated Ohmic contacts, we eliminate external parasitic delays and directly capture the intrinsic interfacial photoresponse in unencapsulated TMDCs under zero bias. The devices achieve ultrafast relaxation lifetimes of 48.5 ps in MoS2/Au and 14.2 ps in MoSe2/Ag, translating to intrinsic 3-dB bandwidths of 4.4 GHz and 7.5 GHz, respectively. Spatial scanning and bias-dependent measurements show that this response is position-independent and bias-immune, ruling out conventional drift-limited transport and identifying hot-carrier super-diffusion driven by an interfacial electron temperature gradient as the operative mechanism. Furthermore, ultrafast pump-probe spectroscopy reveals that the macroscopic response time is quantitatively synchronized with the microscopic optical-to-acoustic phonon scattering lifetime governed by the intrinsic phonon bottleneck. Our findings establish phonon engineering as a viable paradigm to tailor non-equilibrium optoelectronic dynamics, offering a blueprint for zero-bias, ultrafast, self-powered devices.
summary: This work investigates the ultrafast speed limits in 2D TMDCs by using specialized zero-bias terahertz sampling. The authors demonstrate that the rapid carrier response is not limited by conventional drift but by hot-carrier super-diffusion, which is ultimately governed by the intrinsic phonon bottleneck. This establishes phonon engineering as a key paradigm for designing faster, self-powered optoelectronic devices.
main_problem: The operational speed of 2D TMDCs for optoelectronics is limited by low room-temperature mobilities and carrier transit delays.
main_result: The ultrafast response is governed by hot-carrier super-diffusion, which is quantitatively synchronized with the intrinsic optical-to-acoustic phonon scattering lifetime (phonon bottleneck).
method: The study uses on-chip terahertz optoelectronic sampling at zero bias to measure intrinsic photoresponse, complemented by ultrafast pump-probe spectroscopy.
model_or_system: The system involves 2D TMDCs ($	ext{MoS}_2$, $	ext{MoSe}_2$) interfaced with metal contacts, studied under zero-bias conditions to isolate intrinsic carrier dynamics from drift-limited transport.

main_assumptions: The measurement setup successfully eliminates external parasitic delays and electric-field-driven drift by using Ohmic contacts and zero bias.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate time-resolved photocurrents, comparing Ohmic vs. Schottky contacts, showing position and bias independence of the fast decay component, and correlating optical phonon lifetimes with macroscopic electrical relaxation times.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the limitations of TMDCs, details the specialized zero-bias measurement platform, presents evidence ruling out drift-limited transport (via Ohmic/Schottky comparison), identifies hot-carrier super-diffusion, and finally links the macroscopic speed limit to the microscopic phonon bottleneck.
why_interesting: While focused on solid-state electronics, the explicit identification of the phonon bottleneck as the rate-limiting step for non-equilibrium carrier dynamics provides a direct, measurable link between lattice vibrations and device performance, relevant to open quantum system modeling.
